column1: # print-ledger.tsv — what paper EXISTS, one line per print job.
# This is the file `day-guard.sh` reads to answer "does paper for this day already
# exist?" — Guard C, the one that stops a morning from reprinting a sheet that is
# already sitting in the stack. It is TRACKED IN GIT on purpose: a gitignored
# ledger starts empty on a fresh clone, and an empty ledger silently answers "no
# paper exists" for every day, which is the exact wrong answer.
# ⚠️ DO NOT hand-edit this file with a grep filter. On 2026-07-31 a cleanup pass
# ran `grep -v "logic$"` over it to strip test rows and silently deleted four real
# seed rows — every worksheet whose name ends in "-logic". Rewrite the whole file
# from a known source instead, then re-run ./test-day-guard.sh, which counts the
# rows per day and will catch exactly that.
# Rows dated before 2026-07-31 are RECONSTRUCTED from CUPS job history (jobs
# schedule table. Job COUNTS and DATES are measured and exact. The mapping of a
# specific job number to a specific filename is inferred from the plan — CUPS no
# longer exposes job titles here. Fine for the guard, which only reads target_day,
# but don't treat a label below as evidence of what a given job contained.
# Everything from 2026-07-31 onward is recorded live by day-guard.sh at print time.

column1: # 2026-08-01 (2): the MANUAL PRINT row above was sent from Preview/Chrome, not through
# print-drill.sh, so no guard saw it and nothing would have recorded it. Added by hand
# from CUPS (job 166, completed 16:15:44) — the ledger's job is to say what paper
# EXISTS, and a row missing here reads as "no paper" to tomorrow's Guard C.
# It is kid2's REDO of the Aug 1 division drill: he produced answers with no written
# work, so the redo moved to a grid/prompts sheet where each step has its own box.
# 2026-08-16: ONE day's paper (Block 2 opener), not four items. The two identical
# division-drill rows are the SAME sheet — job 169 was cancelled in the queue before
# anything reached paper and replaced by job 170. Reason: 169 printed UNDATED, because
# print-worksheet.sh's --date pattern required the worksheet template's <div>Date: shape
# and drill_gen.py emits Date: inside a flex .meta row. The stamper was loosened the same
# hour, so job 170 carries "August 16, 2026". Zero sheets were spent on 169 — the printer
# was offline for the whole window, which is the only reason the swap was free.
# Also on 2026-08-16: the printer is a NETWORK queue (dnssd://…_ipp._tcp), not USB. Jobs
# 167/168/170 sat queued with "offline-report" until it rejoined the network. `lp`
# returning a request id means CUPS ACCEPTED the job; it says nothing about paper.
